chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Al-Halby, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the injuries of men and women regarding the blood money (diyah) and retaliation (qisas). He said: 'Men and women are equal in retaliation; the tooth for the tooth, the fracture for the fracture, and the finger for the finger are equal, until the injuries reach one-third of the blood money. When they exceed one-third, the blood money of the man regarding the injuries becomes two-thirds of the blood money, and the blood money of the woman becomes one-third of the blood money.'

key_terms.الدِّيَاتِ: Blood money (compensation for injury or death)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in blood money for men and women regarding major injuries in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential principle of 'al-sin bi al-sin' (equal for equal) in Qisas, establishing that gender equality in retaliation applies up to one-third of the total Diyah. Beyond this threshold, the compensation shifts to the standard male-to-female ratio of 2:1, a nuance that distinguishes between the value of the soul in retaliation versus the fixed monetary compensation for major injuries. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for understanding the transition from strict equivalence to proportional compensation in cases of severe bodily harm.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Al Halby who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was asked about injuries of the men and the women regarding the wergild and the retaliation, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The men and the women regarding the retaliation are equal, the tooth with the tooth, and the fracture with the fracture, and the finger with the finger, same, until the injuries reach a third of the wergild. So when it exceeds the third, the wergild of the men with regards to the injuries become two-third of the wergild and a wergild of the women, a one-third of the wergild’.
